newsitem.title: USA: Pan Am, Carnival Air set news conference.
newsitem.headline: Pan Am, Carnival Air set news conference.

text.p: Pan Am Corp and Carnival Air Lines will hold a joint news conference on Friday morning to discuss the acquisition of Carnival, officials with the two companies said on Thursday.
"The subject will be the acquisition of Carnival," said Pan Am spokesman Jeff Kriendler. He declined to say if the two companies would announce an agreement by Pan Am to acquire Carnival.
The news conference was scheduled for 1100 EST (1600 GMT) on Friday at Pan Am's Miami offices.
Carnival owner Micky Arison, chief executive of leading cruise ship operator Carnival Corp., and Martin Shugrue, founder of the start-up Pan Am, will attend, Kriendler said.

Pan Am on Wednesday said it was open to acquisitions and other opportunities to expand its four-jet Pan American World Airways. But officials for both companies declined to confirm reports that the two had restarted acquisition talks.
Last July, Pan Am agreed to pay about $100 million for Carnival Air. But the transaction was called off after Pan Am examined the carrier's books and sought to rework terms.

A combination of Pan Am and Carnival Air would create a much larger regional airline with a total of 31 jets and more than 2,200 employees. Annual revenues would be an estimated $400 million, with operations centered in south Florida.
